title: DevEx Docs Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Top Support Fixes
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines conventions, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and production-ready docs that reduce developer time-to-first-success with Redwood Inference and lower support load through clear troubleshooting guidance.

Scope:
- SDK reference guides (Python, TypeScript, Go where applicable)
- Quickstarts and one-file templates (serverless, backend, client)
- API example snippets (REST/cURL, Python, JS)
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, versioning, rollback, metrics)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained as living content

Owners and Contacts:
- Primary owner: DevEx Technical Writing (engineering)
- Secondary owner: SDK Engineering team
- On-call reviewer for publishing issues: devex-oncall@redwoodinference.internal
- Document steward: Ava Martinez (author)

Standards and Style (must follow):
1) Tone and audience: engineering-first, concise, action-oriented. Assume readers are software/ML engineers and platform teams.
2) Structure: each page must include: Short summary, When to use, Prerequisites, Step-by-step, Example code, Troubleshooting, Related pages, Changelog.
3) Headings: use H1 for title, H2 for major sections, H3 for subsections. Keep content scannable with bullets and numbered steps.
4) Code: provide runnable examples. For SDKs include pip/npm install commands and minimal imports.
5) Licensing and links: link to model catalog, API reference, and relevant ADRs.

SDK Guides: minimum checklist for every SDK page:
- Quick summary (1-2 sentences)
- Supported versions and compatibility table (SDK vs API vs runtime)
- Install instructions (package manager commands)
- Auth and configuration examples (env vars, config objects)
- Core usage examples: init client, request examples, streaming example (if supported)
- Error handling section with common exceptions and recommended retries/backoff
- API surface map linking to Reference pages
- Tests and CI snippets (unit tests showing mock usage)

Example (Python SDK snippet):
```
# Install
pip install redwood-inference

# Minimal example
from redwood_inference import Client

client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-7b", prompt="Summarize the release notes in one paragraph.")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates (standard templates to maintain)
- User onboarding quickstart: create API key, call simple generate, show streaming.
- Backend template: Flask/FastAPI example with Redwood client, basic caching and error handling.
- Frontend snippet: Fetch streaming tokens via backend proxy with SSE.
- Embeddings & semantic search template: store embeddings in vector DB, nearest-neighbor example.
- Canary rollout template: deploy two model routes and route X% traffic for experiments.

Template naming conventions:
- Use kebab-case, short descriptive name, include language and year: e.g. redwood-backend-fastapi-template-2026
- Each template must include README, run instructions, env example (.env.sample) and test script.

API Examples: guidelines and canonical snippets
- Provide at least: cURL/REST, Python SDK, JavaScript/TS SDK sample for each major doc flow (generate, chat, embeddings, function calling).
- Preference: show both blocking and streaming examples where applicable.
- Response sizes and token counting: include a short note on cost and token estimation for the example.

Example cURL (text generation):
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"Write a friendly welcome email to a new user."}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publishing lifecycle)
1) Branching: create branch docs/<short-feature>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.
2) Drafting: include metadata header at top of doc (title, summary, owners).
3) Review: submit PR against main/docs-site with reviewers from DevEx and SDK teams. At least one SDK engineer must approve SDK examples.
4) CI checks (automated): link validation, snippet execution smoke tests for Python/JS, spellcheck, and front-end render check.
5) Publishing: merge after approvals; docs deployment occurs automatically via CI to staging. Staging preview must be smoke-tested by author within 24 hours.
6) Rollout: promote to production site on the next scheduled docs deployment window (usually nightly). For high-priority fixes, request hotfix deployment and notify #devex in Slack.
7) Rollback: follow site runbook with step to revert commit and redeploy. Document the rollback in a PR comment and in postmortem if rollback was customer-impacting.

Changelog and Versioning
- Add a Changelog section at bottom of each doc page with date, author, and short summary of changes.
- For SDK breaking changes, add a prominent banner and migration guide.

Metrics and SLAs for Docs Content
- Target: 72-hour median time to first response on doc-related support tickets after major doc changes for the first 30 days.
- Documentation coverage metric: 100% of public SDK surfaces must have at least one working example.
- Docs health check: weekly broken-link report and monthly snippet-execution pass rate (>=95%).

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (living section - keep concise)
1) "Invalid API key / 401"
   - Symptoms: 401 errors on first API call, empty response.
   - Cause: API key not set or using key from a different environment.
   - Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, ensure key has correct scope, show sample export command.
   - Example fix command: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-prod-XXXXX`

2) "Token limits / 413 or truncated outputs"
   - Symptoms: server returns 413 or outputs cut off after N tokens.
   - Cause: request context + max_tokens exceed model limit.
   - Canonical fix: Add prompt trimming guidance, set max_tokens param appropriately, and recommend using streaming for long outputs.

3) "Slow cold-start / high latency on first requests"
   - Symptoms: first request after idle takes 5-15s, subsequent requests faster.
   - Cause: model warm-up / VM scheduling.
   - Canonical fix: Recommend keepalives for low-latency SLOs, use Dedicated pools for production-critical routes. Include sample keepalive schedule with curl hitting /health every 60s.

4) "Embedding mismatch between SDK and server"
   - Symptoms: similarity searches return unexpected results after SDK upgrade.
   - Cause: default embedding model changed or tokenization differences.
   - Canonical fix: Pin embedding model in code and update vector indexing pipeline. Provide migration steps and small evaluation prompt set.

5) "Rate limit / 429"
   - Symptoms: intermittent 429 responses during traffic spikes.
   - Cause: quota or burst exceeded.
   - Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff (base 500ms, max 30s), request quota increase if customer requires sustained throughput.

Maintaining Canonical Fixes:
- Each top-issue entry must include: Symptoms, Cause, Step-by-step Fix, Example commands/snippets, Owner, and Last validated date.
- Owners must revalidate fixes quarterly and after any related runtime changes.

Publishing checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Title & summary present
- [ ] Owners and reviewers listed
- [ ] Code snippets tested locally (or via CI smoke tests)
- [ ] Related pages linked
- [ ] Labels and metadata filled
- [ ] Changelog entry prepared

Emergency docs/edit process:
- For anything customer-impacting (post on status page, updated doc within 2 hours): create hotfix branch, skip non-essential checks (only if CI snippet smoke-tests pass), merge and notify #devex and #support. Record action in incident ticket.

Retention and archival:
- Docs older than 24 months with no updates must be reviewed for archival. Academic or experimental drafts should be marked `draft` or moved to Google Drive.

Appendix: Example FastAPI backend template snippet (minimal)
```
# app.py (FastAPI)
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood_inference import Client

app = FastAPI()
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")

@app.post('/generate')
async def generate(payload: dict):
    resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-7b', prompt=payload.get('prompt',''))
    return {"text": resp.text}
```

Owner note: This playbook is a living document. Authors and owners are responsible for keeping examples current with SDK releases and runtime changes. Use the related_pages links to find supporting runbooks, release notes, and ADRs.

Changelog:
